# TanStack Charts documentation map

TanStack Charts is a small TypeScript visualization grammar inspired by
Observable Plot. It is not a chart-type component library and does not require
a series-shaped data model. D3 is the authoritative algorithm layer. TanStack
owns the grammar, responsive scene compiler, renderers, and host lifecycle.

Read in this order:

1. README.md — package purpose, imports, implemented surface
2. docs/AI-GUIDE.md — task router and generation rules
3. docs/recipes.md — common chart and composition patterns
4. docs/dynamic-charts.md — state, memoization, preparation, animation
5. docs/responsive-theme-accessibility.md — container sizing, dark mode, UX
6. docs/custom-marks.md — inversion of control and scene protocol
7. docs/bundle-and-performance.md — import topology and performance rules
8. docs/observable-plot-migration.md — concept mapping and compatibility
9. docs/tanstack-stats-migration.md — production parity scope and migration gate

Hard rules:

- Keep chart definitions stable, normally at module scope.
- Pass application state through one typed input object.
- Use the original data directly; do not normalize it into library-owned series.
- Use field channels for simple properties and accessors for derived values.
- Give every dynamic or reorderable datum a stable key.
- Compose marks in one definition instead of switching to a custom chart API.
- Put data exploration, cleaning, and chart recommendation in tooling or skills,
  not the runtime library.
- Omit width for container-responsive charts. Set initialWidth for deterministic
  SSR when the server cannot know the container width.
- Always provide ariaLabel; add ariaDescription when the chart needs context.
- Use subpath imports when enforcing a hard bundle boundary.
- Supply configured D3 positional scales. Let TanStack own their responsive
  pixel ranges and D3 own domains, mapping, ticks, and formatting.
- For an application-owned cursor, brush, or zoom, import focusDisabled from
  @tanstack/charts/focus/disabled and keep native datum focus out of the path.
- Invert interaction coordinates by copying the configured D3 scale onto the
  resolved scene.chart range. Apply explicit date or numeric rounding after
  inversion; do not reimplement scale math.
- Supply D3 color and radius scales directly when those channels need mapping.
- Use named imports from granular d3-* packages, never the d3 umbrella.
- Add curves through d3Curve(curveFactory) so straight marks do not import
  d3-shape.
- Let mark data infer channel fields and callback datum types. Introduce only
  the dynamic Input type with defineChart<Input>().
- Never use as any, double assertions, suppression comments, private imports,
  or adapter generics to force chart code through TypeScript.
- Treat installed TanStack Charts declarations and local recipes as
  authoritative. Observable Plot documentation is conceptual and does not
  imply that a Plot option exists here.
- Dynamic React, Octane, and vanilla hosts require input. Static definitions
  reject it.
- Read semantic values from point.datum. Narrow heterogeneous datum unions and
  broad coordinate values with ordinary TypeScript guards.
